name: Thapong Visual Arts Centre
funding: Board-run centre funded by the Ministry of Youth, Sport and Culture (P2.2M for the 2014 refit). Partners: HB Botswana (2024), BTC Foundation (2018), DTC Botswana and FNB Foundation (2014).
watch: De Beers gave P75,000 toward the 2014 refit. That is twelve years old and not a current funding line.
records_note: No website of its own was found; news items name partners and a 2014 board chair, but no reports, accounts or current board are public.

name: Instituto Tunga
funding: Artist's estate institute. The Tunga catalogue raisonné it leads is sponsored by Itaú and Sabesp under the Rouanet Law.
watch: The researcher's Itaú Cultural credit is wrong: the catalogue page names the bank Itaú and the state water utility Sabesp.
records_note: Its own site institutotunga.org showed a maintenance notice, so reports, accounts, funders and board were not checked.

name: Museu de Arte Brasileira da FAAP
funding: Kept by the private university foundation FAAP, created in 1947 from the Penteado estate. The 2026 MAM show runs on Lei Rouanet and São Paulo's PROMAC; no company is named.
records_note: The museum's page and its parent foundation FAAP's legal page post no annual report, accounts, sponsor list or board.

name: Sesc São Paulo
funding: 2023 revenue R$3.44bn: R$2.70bn (78%) from the compulsory levy on commerce, services and tourism firms, R$209M from services, R$495M financial income.
records_note: Posts annual management reports for 2020 to 2024 with an independent audit report; funded by a business levy and names no sponsors.

name: doual'art
funding: Independent non-profit (1991) relying on international grant-makers and sponsors.
watch: Runs the SUD Salon Urbain de Douala; roster not public.
records_note: Its site footer names five supporters, including Arts Collaboratory and Brot für die Welt, but undated; no annual report, accounts or board are posted.

name: He Art Museum
funding: Private, founded by the family of Midea's founder (appliance manufacturing).
watch: Founding money is Midea's; TBIJ (29 May 2025) reported Midea-run factories took part in the Uyghur labour-transfer scheme.
why_flagged: Founding money is Midea's; TBIJ (29 May 2025) reported Midea-run factories took part in the Uyghur labour-transfer scheme.
records_note: He Art Museum's site shows exhibitions, collection and visiting details, but no reports, accounts, donor list or board.

name: Hubei Museum of Art
funding: Provincial public museum under the Hubei Dept of Culture and Tourism, funded through the provincial budget (2026 unit budget filed).
watch: Roster not checked. The provincial finance portal holding the 2026 budget (czt.hubei.gov.cn) blocked access, so the funding lines went unread.
records_note: Publishes no reports, funders or board; its parent department lists its 2026 unit budget on the provincial budget portal, with no final accounts.

name: Museum of Contemporary Art Yinchuan
funding: Founded 2012-15 by Ningxia Minsheng Real Estate (property developer) with the provincial government under a BOT deal; about 300m yuan build.
watch: Founder link and roster not verified.
records_note: The museum's website could not be opened, so its reports, accounts, funders and board stay unchecked.

name: Fragmentos, Espacio de Arte y Memoria
funding: Colombian Ministry of Culture space run by the Museo Nacional.
watch: In May 2021 President Duque held a political meeting in the space; Francis Alÿs withdrew his show and Doris Salcedo protested.
why_flagged: Colombian Ministry of Culture space run by the Museo Nacional. Entry is free and no private sponsor is named.
records_note: The space's own site publishes no reports, accounts, sponsor list or board; it sits under the Ministry of Culture and Museo Nacional.

name: Museo de Arte y Diseño Contemporáneo
funding: Agency of Costa Rica's Ministry of Culture, paid through the national budget. Budget pages are online for 2013 to 2020.
watch: The complex belongs to the Centro Nacional de Cultura.
records_note: A ministry agency: posts management reports from 1992 to 2022, financial statements for 2013 to 2019 and budgets to 2020; no funder list or board.

name: Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes de La Habana
funding: State museum subordinate to Cuba's Ministry of Culture.
watch: The October 2021 boycott letter targets the Havana Biennial and the government, not this museum.
records_note: Its official site could not be reached from here, so reports, accounts, funders and board could not be checked.

name: DOX Centre for Contemporary Art
funding: Private centre founded by Leoš Válka (property).
records_note: Posts annual reports for 2014 to 2016, with accounting statements in the 2015 one, and shows undated partner logos; no board list.
